name: Ammut (African Monsters (PF1))
body:
AMMUT
CR 17/MR 7

This lumbering beast is a horrifying amalgam of leonine foreparts and the hindquarters of a hippopotamus, with the gaping maw of a savage crocodile. Its eyes are a dead black and a hungry, swirling darkness roils forth from its gullet when it roars a challenge.

XP 102,400
NE Huge magical beast (extraplanar, mythic)
Init +1; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +29
Aura stench (DC 29, 1d10 minutes)

DEFENSE

AC 34, touch 9, flat-footed 33 (+4 armor, +1 Dex, +21 natural, -2 size)
hp 360 (20d10+250)
Fort +21, Ref +13, Will +12
Defensive Abilities beyond judgment, shed skin; DR 10/epic; Immune disease, poison, death effects, energy drain, fear, negative energy, necromantic effects

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., burrow 20 ft., swim 30 ft.; sprint
Melee bite +28 (4d6+10/15-20/x3 plus energy drain and grab), 2 claws +28 (1d8+10)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 15 ft.
Special Attacks death roll, heart-eater, soul devourer, reverberating roar M, taste of judgment, augmented critical, energy drain (1 level levels, DC 26), fast swallow, fear cone (60 ft., DC 26), swallow whole (4d6 bludgeoning and slashing and 2 negative levels damage, AC 20, 36 hp)

STATISTICS

Str 31, Dex 13, Con 28, Int 17, Wis 22, Cha 22
Base Atk +20; CMB +32; CMD 43 (47 vs. trip)
Feats Bleeding Critical, Cleave, Combat Reflexes, Critical Focus, Great Cleave, Improved Critical (bite), Inescapable Grasp, Power Attack, Staggering Critical, Stunning Assault, MF, Stunning Critical
Skills Climb +20, Intimidate +26, Knowledge (religion) +15, Perception +29, Sense Motive +26, Survival +26, Swim +22
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Infernal, Pharaonic
SQ amphibious

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Augmented Critical (Ex)

An ammut has a critical threat range of 18-20 and a critical multiplier of x3 with its bite.

Beyond Judgment (Ex)

An ammut is an instrument of divine judgment and inexorable punishment and as an agent of divine justice it is untouchable by the judgment and vengeance of mortals. Abilities or effects that depend on a creature’s type or alignment have no effect on an ammut, and sacred, profane, and luck bonuses do not apply against an ammut. Whenever it is targeted with a curse or compulsion, it can expend one use of its mythic power as an immediate action to cause that effect to rebound on its creator rather than affecting the ammut. This functions as spell turning, but it can affect even area effects or effects delivered by touch. Any other targets or creatures in the area of that effect are affected normally.

Death Roll (Ex)

When grappling a foe of its size or smaller, an ammut can perform a death roll upon making a successful grapple check. As it clings to its foe, it tucks in its legs and rolls rapidly, twisting and wrenching its victim. The ammut inflicts its bite damage and knocks the creature prone. If successful, the ammut maintains its grapple.

Fear Cone (Su)

An ammut can trigger its fear cone as a standard action, or as a swift action immediately after it uses its reverberating roar or swallows a creature whole.

Hearteater (Ex)

Whenever an ammut confirms a critical hit with its bite, it can expend one use of its mythic power to attempt to tear out the heart of a humanoid foe, killing it instantly (DC 29 Fort negates). The save DC is Constitution-based and the target gains a +2 bonus on this saving throw if wearing medium armor, +4 if wearing heavy armor. A creature with a natural armor bonus to AC also gains a bonus on this saving throw equal to one-half its natural armor bonus.

Whenever an ammut successfully uses this ability, or whenever it kills a creature with its bite, all living creatures within 30 feet are frightened for 1 round. A successful DC 26 Will save negates this effect for mythic creatures or reduces it to shaken for non-mythic creatures. This is a mind-affecting fear effect, and the save DC is Charisma-based.

Reverberating Roar (Su)

As a standard action, an ammut can unleash a devastating roar that deals 12d8 points of sonic damage (DC 29 Fortitude half) in a 30-foot cone-shaped burst, and the deafening echoes of this sonic blast reverberate within the area for 7 rounds, dealing 2d8 points of sonic damage (DC 27 Reflex half). Creatures failing a saving throw against the ammut’s roar are deafened for 1 hour. If they fail a second save, they are staggered for 7 rounds. A third or subsequent failed save causes a creature to become stunned for 1 round. An ammut must wait 1d4 rounds in between uses of its roar; however, it can expend one use of its mythic power to reduce this interval to 1 round.

Shed Skin (Ex)

As a swift action, an ammut that begins its turn affected by any ongoing effect can end that effect by causing its skin to tear open and slough off in bloody shreds. This deals 2 points of Constitution damage to the ammut but ends the effect immediately and allows the ammut to make a single Intimidate check to demoralize all creatures it threatens that have line of sight to it when it sheds its skin. If the ongoing effect is a mythic effect, the ammut must expend one use of mythic power to use this ability.

Soul Devourer (Su)

When an ammut reduces a target below 0 hit points, the target must succeed on a DC 29 Fortitude save or die; this is a death effect, and if the target fails its save the ammut gains the benefit of a death knell spell (caster level 20th). In addition, whenever an ammut kills a creature it can expend one use of its mythic power as a free action to affect the target as rest eternal (caster level 20th).

Sprint (Ex)

Once per minute an ammut may sprint, increasing its land speed to 60 feet for 1 round.

Taste of Judgment (Su)

An ammut is an instrument of divine judgment, and those it has marked for doom can escape it only with great difficulty. Whenever an ammut inflicts a negative level upon a target, it can designate that target as its quarry, as the ranger class feature. This increases the DC of saving throws to remove the negative level by 2, and any non-mythic effect that normally removes negative levels fails unless the caster succeeds at a caster level check against the same DC. If all negative levels possessed by an ammut’s quarry are removed, the effects of the quarry ability are negated. An ammut can have only a single mythic quarry at a time, but it can designate up to seven nonmythic creatures as its quarry simultaneously.

ECOLOGY

Environment any underground (Abaddon, Abyss, or Hell)
Organization solitary
Treasure double standard

Ammuts have an unsettling grace to their movements, stalking with jarring yet fluid steps, as if all the animal likenesses it possesses are controlled by a chaotic, serpentine power.

Their powerful reptilian mouths contain elongated teeth with jaws adorned by the shredded flesh of their victim’s remains. Shadows swirl about from the hollows of their skull and capture no light or reflection. The ammut’s inky black eyes are depthless, locking their gaze upon their prey with a transfixed fierceness as it weighs every transgression of the soul.

Everyone has a moral deficit to answer for and no one is pure, and when an ammut catches the scent of iniquity it can focus on nothing else.

There is no escaping their demand for ultimate judgment and their ravenous for a sinner’s heart, and those whose hearts are devoured by an ammut are consumed in spirit as well as in body, obliterated as if they had never been. Ammuts are virtually immortal, never succumbing to old age. A fully grown ammut is over 20 feet long and 10 feet high at the shoulder and weighs 5 tons.

Through its massive, muscular torso, one can see the beating of the beast’s heart; larger than it should be and so loud the noise of it collides inside the listener’s skull, making it difficult to think of anything outside the pounding rhythm.

Those hearing this frightful thrumming, even should they manage to escape the ammut’s devouring jaws, are forever restless, with every quiet moment haunted by its dirge-like phantom pulse.

Ammuts gain substance from the hearts of their victims.

They are never satiated and have a relentless compulsion to prey upon those who deserve gruesome judgment. These called ‘Eaters of Hearts’ have no interest in mingling with their own kind and are loners by nature. All ammuts are female but do not reproduce in any conventional sense, instead being created by the goddess Ma’at, the embodiment of order, balance, morality, and justice, from souls that have great spiritual yearnings unresolved from life. By the laws of ma’at that rule mortals and immortals alike, she could not allow these souls to cross to the afterlife so unfulfilled, and in communion with the powers of death Ma’at recognized there would be no better judgment of one’s actions than from those who still yearn for retribution. Souls transformed into ravening beasts become instruments of judgment and justice, devouring the hearts of those not pure enough to warrant continued existence in life or the afterlife. Their attributes are that of the most ferocious beasts: the powerful forelimbs of a lion, the giant maw of the crocodile, and the thunderous hindquarters of the hippopotamus.

Ammuts dwell underground and are drawn to thermal locations such as volcanic activity or fiery underground lakes. They are adept at burrowing to create a sheltered den in which to hide. They are also partially aquatic, often floating with only their black eyes breaking the surface to observe their surroundings. Although they represent judgmental annihilation, ammuts are not truly evil creatures who can control their actions by choice. They are driven by an undying and unquenchable need to devour wrongdoing and to right the imbalance of actions and misdeeds unpaid.

Unfortunately, no mortal is truly without blemish, and over the long millennia ammuts have heard every possible prevarication and rationalization to justify a mortal’s action, to the point where few are willing to give a fair hearing to those crossing their path. Assuming all who come before them are already guilty, ammuts are all too happy to dispense with judgment and jump straight to the execution.
